$fxv#0.name: ASIM - Discord CDN Risky File Download (Zscaler ZIA)
$fxv#0.displayName: ASIM - Discord CDN Risky File Download (Zscaler ZIA)
$fxv#0.description:
'Identifies callouts to Discord CDN addresses for risky file extensions. This detection triggers when a
callout for a risky file is made to a Discord server that has only been seen once in the environment.
Unique Discord servers are identified using the server ID embedded in the request URL (DiscordServerId in
the query). Discord CDN has been used in multiple campaigns to download additional payloads.
Adapted from the upstream Zscaler Internet Access rule "Discord CDN Risky File Download"
(original id 010bd98c-a6be-498c-bdcd-502308c0fdae) to use the ASIM Web Session normalized schema
(_Im_WebSession) instead of CommonSecurityLog, so it works with any source normalized to ASIM,
including a Cribl Stream pipeline that maps Zscaler ZIA logs to _Im_WebSession.'
$fxv#0.query:
let connectionThreshold = 1;
let riskyExtensions = dynamic([".bin", ".exe", ".dll", ".msi"]);
_Im_WebSession
| where EventVendor =~ "Zscaler" and EventProduct has "ZIA"
| where Url has_any ("media.discordapp.net", "cdn.discordapp.com")
| where Url has "attachments"
| where DvcAction != "Deny"
| extend DiscordServerId = extract(@"/attachments/([0-9]+)/", 1, Url)
| where isnotempty(DiscordServerId)
| summarize
    dcount(Url),
    make_set(SrcUsername),
    make_set(SrcIpAddr),
    make_set(Url),
    min(TimeGenerated),
    max(TimeGenerated),
    make_set(DvcAction)
    by DiscordServerId
| where dcount_Url <= connectionThreshold
| mv-expand set_SrcUsername to typeof(string), set_Url to typeof(string), set_DvcAction to typeof(string), set_SrcIpAddr to typeof(string)
| summarize by DiscordServerId, dcount_Url, set_SrcUsername, min_TimeGenerated, max_TimeGenerated, set_DvcAction, set_SrcIpAddr, set_Url
| project
    StartTime = min_TimeGenerated,
    EndTime = max_TimeGenerated,
    DeviceActionTaken = set_DvcAction,
    SourceUser = set_SrcUsername,
    SourceIP = set_SrcIpAddr,
    RequestUrl = set_Url
| where RequestUrl has_any (riskyExtensions)

$fxv#0.name: ASIM - Request for Single Resource on Domain (Zscaler ZIA)
$fxv#0.displayName: ASIM - Request for Single Resource on Domain (Zscaler ZIA)
$fxv#0.description:
'Looks for connections to a domain where only a single resource is requested. This is unusual because most
modern web applications require additional resources (scripts, images, style sheets, and so on) beyond the
first request. This pattern is often associated with malware beaconing or with tracking URLs delivered in
email. Developed for Zscaler but applicable to any outbound web logging normalized to ASIM.
Adapted from the upstream Zscaler Internet Access rule "Request for single resource on domain"
(original id 4d500e6d-c984-43a3-9f39-7edec8dcc04d) to use the ASIM Web Session normalized schema
(_Im_WebSession) instead of CommonSecurityLog, so it works with any source normalized to ASIM,
including a Cribl Stream pipeline that maps Zscaler ZIA logs to _Im_WebSession.'
$fxv#0.query:
let scriptExtensions = dynamic([".php", ".aspx", ".asp", ".cfml"]);
// The number of distinct URLs seen for the domain; higher = less likely to be suspicious
let uriThreshold = 1;
_Im_WebSession
| where EventVendor =~ "Zscaler" and EventProduct has "ZIA"
// Only look at connections that were allowed through the web proxy
| where DvcAction == "Allow"
// Only look where some data was actually exchanged
| where SrcBytes > 0 and DstBytes > 0
| extend Domain = iff(countof(DstHostname, '.') >= 2, strcat(split(DstHostname, '.')[-2], '.', split(DstHostname, '.')[-1]), DstHostname)
| extend GetData = iff(Url has "?", 1, 0)
| summarize
    StartTimeUtc = min(TimeGenerated),
    EndTimeUtc = max(TimeGenerated),
    make_list(Url),
    make_list(DstIpAddr),
    make_list(SrcIpAddr),
    numOfConnections = count(),
    make_set(HttpRequestMethod),
    max(GetData),
    max(HttpReferrer)
    by Domain
// Determine the number of distinct URLs visited for the domain
| extend destinationURI = arraylength(list_Url)
| where destinationURI <= uriThreshold
| where tostring(list_Url) has_any (scriptExtensions)
// Remove matches with a referrer (legitimate click-through browsing traffic)
| where isempty(max_HttpReferrer)
// Keep requests where data was transferred, either via a GET with parameters or a POST
| where set_HttpRequestMethod has "POST" or max_GetData == 1
// Defeat email click tracking; may increase false negatives while decreasing false positives
| where tostring(list_Url) !has "click" and set_HttpRequestMethod !has "GET"
| mv-expand list_Url, list_DstIpAddr
| extend RequestUrl = tostring(list_Url), DestinationIP = tostring(list_DstIpAddr), ClientIP = tostring(list_SrcIpAddr)
| project-away list_Url, list_DstIpAddr, list_SrcIpAddr, destinationURI, Domain, StartTimeUtc, EndTimeUtc, max_GetData, max_HttpReferrer

$fxv#0.name: ASIM - Zscaler Shared ZPA Session (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.displayName: ASIM - Zscaler Shared ZPA Session (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.description:
'Detects a shared Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) session, that is, the same user establishing a new session
from a different source IP address before their previous session has ended. This can indicate credential
sharing or session hijacking.
Adapted from the upstream Zscaler Private Access rule "Zscaler - Shared ZPA session"
(original id 40a98355-0e52-479f-8c91-4ab659cba878, ZPAEvent table) to use the ASIM Authentication
normalized schema (_Im_Authentication) instead of the raw ZPAEvent table. ZPA session establishment and
termination is treated as Logon/Logoff activity for the connecting user (SrcUserName in the raw ZPAEvent
table is mapped to TargetUsername in the Authentication schema, since it identifies the user who signed
in). Assumes a Cribl Stream pipeline maps ZPA session-open events to EventType "Logon" and session-close
events to EventType "Logoff" in _Im_Authentication.
Optimized to invoke the _Im_Authentication unifying parser exactly once per execution: it is materialized
into a single bounded result set (materialize(), filtered to the Zscaler ZPA product predicate) and the
open-session and closed-session branches are both derived from that materialized set, rather than each
querying _Im_Authentication directly. Referencing a unifying ASIM parser more than once in the same query
causes the engine to re-expand the underlying union of source-specific parsers for every reference, which
can exceed the Log Analytics relational operator tree complexity limit (CRT0015). This is a query-plan
optimization only; detection intent, thresholds, and entity mappings are unchanged.'

$fxv#0.name: ASIM - Zscaler Unexpected Event Count of Rejects by Policy (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.displayName: ASIM - Zscaler Unexpected Event Count of Rejects by Policy (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.description:
'Detects an unexpected event count of Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) connection attempts rejected by policy
for a single user. A high volume of policy-based rejections can indicate an attempt to reach applications
the user is not entitled to, a misconfigured client, or reconnaissance activity.
Adapted from the upstream Zscaler Private Access rule "Zscaler - Unexpected event count of rejects by
policy" (original id 593e3e2a-43ce-11ec-81d3-0242ac130003, ZPAEvent table) to use the ASIM Network Session
normalized schema (_Im_NetworkSession) instead of the raw ZPAEvent table. The raw EventResult value
"REJECTED_BY_POLICY" is normalized to EventResult == "Failure" with DvcAction in ("Deny", "Drop"); the
original raw detail string is expected to be preserved in EventOriginalResultDetails for drill-down.
DstUserName in the raw ZPAEvent table is mapped to SrcUsername in the Network Session schema, since it
identifies the connecting (source) user rather than the destination application.'

$fxv#0.name: ASIM - Zscaler Forbidden Countries (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.description:
'Detects suspicious Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) connections established from countries that are not
expected to originate connections to the environment.
Adapted from the upstream Zscaler Private Access rule "Zscaler - Forbidden countries"
(original id b3d112b4-3e1e-11ec-9bbc-0242ac130002, ZPAEvent table) to use the ASIM Network Session
normalized schema (_Im_NetworkSession) instead of the raw ZPAEvent table. DvcAction == "open" is mapped to
DvcAction == "Allow" (the ASIM enumerated value for a permitted session), and DstUserName in the raw
ZPAEvent table is mapped to SrcUsername, since it identifies the connecting (source) user.'
$fxv#0.query:
let bl_countries = dynamic(['CH', 'RU']); //List of countries from which you do not expect ZPA connections
_Im_NetworkSession
| where EventVendor =~ "Zscaler" and EventProduct has "Private Access"
| where DvcAction == "Allow"
| where SrcGeoCountry in~ (bl_countries)
| extend IPCustomEntity = SrcIpAddr, AccountCustomEntity = SrcUsername

$fxv#0.name: ASIM - Zscaler Unexpected Update Operation (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.displayName: ASIM - Zscaler Unexpected Update Operation (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.description:
'Detects an unexpected version transition recorded in a Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) admin-portal
configuration change. The old and new object values are parsed for expectedVersion/currentVersion pairs
and compared to flag downgrades or otherwise unexpected version values, which can indicate tampering with
ZPA App Connector or client configuration.
Adapted from the upstream Zscaler Private Access rule "Zscaler - Unexpected update operation"
(original id 672e2846-4226-11ec-81d3-0242ac130003, ZPAEvent table) to use the ASIM Audit Event normalized
schema (_Im_AuditEvent) instead of the raw ZPAEvent table. AuditOperationType, AuditOldValue and
AuditNewValue in the raw ZPAEvent table map to Operation, OldValue and NewValue in the Audit Event schema.
The original entity mapping used a Process entity populated from the operation name, which has no standard
schema equivalent and was not a true process identifier; it has been replaced with an Account entity
mapped from ActorUsername (the admin who performed the change), which the Audit Event schema exposes
natively. As in the upstream rule, this analytic evaluates every audit event with a non-empty Operation and
computes VersionCheck for triage; it does not filter on VersionCheck so that all configuration-object
changes remain visible to the analyst.'
$fxv#0.query:
_Im_AuditEvent
| where EventVendor =~ "Zscaler" and EventProduct has "Private Access"
| where isnotempty(Operation)
| extend ExpectedVersion1 = extract(@'(expectedVersion":")([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+\.[0-9]+)', 2, OldValue)
| extend ExpectedVersion2 = extract(@'(expectedVersion":")([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+\.[0-9]+)', 3, OldValue)
| extend NewVersion1 = extract(@'("currentVersion":")([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+\.[0-9]+)', 2, NewValue)
| extend NewVersion2 = extract(@'("currentVersion":")([0-9]+)\.([0-9]+\.[0-9]+)', 3, NewValue)
| extend Comparision1 = iff(tolong(ExpectedVersion2) > tolong(NewVersion2), 'Unexpected version', 'Expected version')
| extend VersionCheck = iff(tolong(ExpectedVersion1) > tolong(NewVersion1), 'Unexpected version', Comparision1)
| project-away ExpectedVersion1, ExpectedVersion2, NewVersion1, NewVersion2, Comparision1
| extend AccountCustomEntity = ActorUsername

$fxv#0.name: ASIM - Zscaler Connections by Dormant User (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.displayName: ASIM - Zscaler Connections by Dormant User (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.description:
'Detects Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) sign-ins by a dormant user, that is, a user who signs in during the
current evaluation window but was not observed signing in successfully during the preceding ~14-day
baseline window. Sign-in activity from a dormant account can indicate use of a stale or compromised
credential.
Adapted from the upstream Zscaler Private Access rule "Zscaler - Connections by dormant user"
(original id 66bc77ee-3e45-11ec-9bbc-0242ac130002, ZPAEvent table) to use the ASIM Authentication
normalized schema (_Im_Authentication) instead of the raw ZPAEvent table. DvcAction == "open" is mapped to
EventType == "Logon" and EventResult == "Success", and DstUserName in the raw ZPAEvent table is mapped to
TargetUsername, since it identifies the signed-in user.
Optimized to invoke the _Im_Authentication unifying parser exactly once per execution: the parser is
materialized into a single bounded result set (materialize(), filtered to the 14-day lookback and the
Zscaler ZPA logon/success predicate), and the baseline and current branches are both derived from that
materialized set, rather than each referencing _Im_Authentication directly. Referencing a unifying ASIM
parser more than once in the same query causes the engine to re-expand the underlying union of
source-specific parsers for every reference, which previously caused this rule to fail Log Analytics
compilation with CRT0015 (relational operator tree complexity exceeded).
Correctness fix (security review): the query previously derived the "active users" baseline from the same
full materialized dataset that the detection branch also scanned, so any user present in the current
window was, by construction, also present in the baseline (its own current sign-in was part of the same
set), and the "!in~ (make_list(...))" filter could never match - the rule was effectively a silent
no-op. The query now splits the single materialized result set into two non-overlapping time slices:
baseline = TimeGenerated between (ago(14d) .. ago(1h)) (approximately the preceding 14 days, ending where
the current slice begins) and current = TimeGenerated > ago(1h) (the most recent hour, matching
queryFrequency). Both windows fit inside the existing 14-day queryPeriod, so no schedule change was
required. A leftanti join keyed on TargetUsername returns only users present in the current slice with no
matching TargetUsername in the baseline slice, replacing the prior global make_list()/"!in~" comparison
(which, even before the overlap bug, compared against a single flattened list rather than doing a
per-user check) with a genuine per-user, non-overlapping-window comparison. Detection intent, severity,
thresholds, and entity mappings are unchanged; the baseline window is now bounded to (ago(14d) ..
ago(1h)) instead of a full 14 days, a difference of one hour that is immaterial to the "not seen in the
last 14 days" detection intent.'

$fxv#0.name: ASIM - Zscaler ZPA Connections by New User (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.displayName: ASIM - Zscaler ZPA Connections by New User (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.description:

window but was not observed signing in during the preceding ~14-day baseline window. A first-seen user
sign-in can indicate onboarding of a new account, but can also indicate use of a newly created or
compromised identity.
Adapted from the upstream Zscaler Private Access rule "Zscaler - ZPA connections by new user"
(original id 236a7ec1-0120-40f2-a157-c1a72dde8bcb, ZPAEvent table) to use the ASIM Authentication
normalized schema (_Im_Authentication) instead of the raw ZPAEvent table. DvcAction == "open" is mapped to
EventType == "Logon" and EventResult == "Success", and DstUserName in the raw ZPAEvent table is mapped to

than once in the same query causes the engine to re-expand the underlying union of source-specific

non-overlapping-window comparison. Detection intent, severity, thresholds, and entity mappings are
unchanged; the baseline window is now bounded to (ago(14d) .. ago(1h)) instead of a full 14 days, a

$fxv#0.name: ASIM - Zscaler ZPA Connections from New Country (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.displayName: ASIM - Zscaler ZPA Connections from New Country (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.description:
'Detects Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) connections from a country that has not been observed for the
connecting user during the preceding ~14-day baseline window. A first-seen source country for a user can
indicate travel, use of an anonymizing proxy or VPN, or account compromise.
Adapted from the upstream Zscaler Private Access rule "Zscaler - ZPA connections from new country"
(original id c4902121-7a7e-44d1-810b-88d26db622ff, ZPAEvent table) to use the ASIM Network Session
normalized schema (_Im_NetworkSession) instead of the raw ZPAEvent table. DvcAction == "open" is mapped to
DvcAction == "Allow" for the baseline, and DstUserName in the raw ZPAEvent table is mapped to SrcUsername,
since it identifies the connecting (source) user. As in the upstream rule, the current-window query is not
filtered to DvcAction == "Allow", so both permitted and denied sessions are evaluated for new-country
activity.
Optimized to invoke the _Im_NetworkSession unifying parser exactly once per execution: it is materialized
into a single bounded result set (materialize(), filtered to the 14-day lookback and the Zscaler ZPA
product predicate), and the baseline and current branches are both derived from that materialized set,
preserving the original asymmetric DvcAction filtering while avoiding a second parser expansion.
Referencing a unifying ASIM parser more than once in the same query causes the engine to re-expand the
underlying union of source-specific parsers for every reference, which can exceed the Log Analytics
relational operator tree complexity limit (CRT0015).
Correctness fix (security review): the query previously (1) derived listCountries from the same full
14-day dataset that the detection branch also scanned, so a country seen for a user in the current window
was, by construction, already part of that same 14-day set; and (2) projected away the SrcUsername grouping
column after make_set(), so "SrcGeoCountry !in (listCountries)" compared against a single flattened list of
every user's countries combined, rather than checking only the current row's own user - a user could be
masked from detection by a completely different user having connected from that country. The query now
splits the materialized result set into two non-overlapping time slices - baseline = TimeGenerated between
(ago(14d) .. ago(1h)) (approximately the preceding 14 days, ending where the current slice begins, and
restricted to DvcAction == "Allow" as before) and current = TimeGenerated > ago(1h) (the most recent hour,
matching queryFrequency, unfiltered on DvcAction as before) - both of which fit inside the existing 14-day
queryPeriod, so no schedule change was required. A leftanti join keyed on (SrcUsername, SrcGeoCountry)
returns only (user, country) pairs present in the current slice with no matching pair in the baseline
slice, so a country is only flagged as new for the specific user who connected from it, and a different
user history can no longer suppress the detection. Detection intent, severity, thresholds, and entity
mappings are unchanged; the baseline window is now bounded to (ago(14d) .. ago(1h)) instead of a full 14
days, a difference of one hour that is immaterial to the "not seen in the last 14 days" detection intent.'

$fxv#0.name: ASIM - Zscaler ZPA Connections Outside Operational Hours (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.displayName: ASIM - Zscaler ZPA Connections Outside Operational Hours (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.description:
'Detects Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) connections established outside the defined operational hours window
(08:00-19:00). Connections outside normal business hours can indicate automated tooling, an attacker in a
different time zone, or use of a compromised account outside the user''s normal working pattern.
Adapted from the upstream Zscaler Private Access rule "Zscaler - ZPA connections outside operational hours"
(original id 2859ad22-46c8-4cc7-ad7b-80ce0cba0af3, ZPAEvent table) to use the ASIM Network Session
normalized schema (_Im_NetworkSession) instead of the raw ZPAEvent table. DvcAction == "open" is mapped to
DvcAction == "Allow", and DstUserName in the raw ZPAEvent table is mapped to SrcUsername, since it
identifies the connecting (source) user. The raw LogTimestamp string field is replaced with the standard
EventStartTime datetime field, removing the need to call todatetime() on a raw string. The upstream
"between" hour range (19 .. 8) was inverted and always evaluated to an empty range; it has been replaced
with the logically equivalent "!between (8 .. 19)" so the rule actually flags connections outside the
08:00-19:00 operational window, which is a direct, schema-driven correction to the original threshold
logic rather than a change in detection intent.'
$fxv#0.query:
_Im_NetworkSession
| where EventVendor =~ "Zscaler" and EventProduct has "Private Access"
| where DvcAction == "Allow"
| where datetime_part("Hour", EventStartTime) !between (8 .. 19)
| summarize count() by SrcUsername
| project SrcUsername
| extend AccountCustomEntity = SrcUsername

$fxv#0.name: ASIM - Zscaler Unexpected ZPA Session Duration (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.displayName: ASIM - Zscaler Unexpected ZPA Session Duration (Zscaler ZPA)
$fxv#0.description:
'Detects a Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) session whose duration exceeds an 8-hour threshold. An unusually
long-lived session can indicate an attacker maintaining persistent access, or a client that failed to
properly close its session.
Adapted from the upstream Zscaler Private Access rule "Zscaler - Unexpected ZPA session duration"
(original id e07846e0-43ad-11ec-81d3-0242ac130003, ZPAEvent table) to use the ASIM Network Session
normalized schema (_Im_NetworkSession) instead of the raw ZPAEvent table. DvcAction "open"/"close" values,
which have no equivalent in the ASIM enumerated DvcAction values (Allow/Deny/Drop/...), are mapped to
EventSubType == "Start" and EventSubType == "End" respectively; ConnectionID in the raw ZPAEvent table is
mapped to NetworkSessionId, the standard schema session correlation key; and DstUserName is mapped to
SrcUsername, since it identifies the connecting (source) user. Assumes a Cribl Stream pipeline emits ZPA
session-open and session-close audit records as two _Im_NetworkSession rows sharing the same
NetworkSessionId. If the pipeline instead emits a single row per completed session, the join below can be
replaced with a direct filter on the NetworkDuration field.
Optimized to invoke the _Im_NetworkSession unifying parser exactly once per execution: it is materialized
into a single bounded result set (materialize(), filtered to the 24-hour lookback and the Zscaler ZPA
product predicate) and both the open-session and closed-session branches are derived from that
materialized set, rather than each querying _Im_NetworkSession directly. Referencing a unifying ASIM
parser more than once in the same query causes the engine to re-expand the underlying union of
source-specific parsers for every reference, which can exceed the Log Analytics relational operator tree
complexity limit (CRT0015). This is a query-plan optimization only; detection intent, thresholds, and
entity mappings are unchanged.'

metadata.title: Zscaler ASIM Incident Response
metadata.description: Microsoft Sentinel incident-triggered Consumption Logic App that enriches an incident with ASIM-normalized network/web session context, requests explicit analyst approval over Microsoft Teams, and - only after approval - blocks the approved IP and URL entities in Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA) through the Zscaler OneAPI OAuth2 gateway. Zscaler OAuth2 credentials are stored in and retrieved from Azure Key Vault via the playbook's managed identity; no secrets are stored in this template.
prerequisites: Deploy this template with WorkflowState left as Disabled (the default). Do not enable the workflow until every prerequisite below is complete.

Create (or reuse) an Azure Key Vault with soft delete and purge protection enabled. Store three secrets in it out-of-band: the Zscaler OneAPI OAuth2 client ID, the OAuth2 client secret, and the full OAuth2 token URL (for example https://<vanity-domain>.zslogin.net/oauth2/v1/token). Never place these values in this template, a parameters file, or source control.

Grant the deployed Logic App's system-assigned managed identity the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role (or an equivalent least-privilege role) scoped to that Key Vault, and the 'Log Analytics Reader' role scoped to the target Log Analytics workspace. This template intentionally does not create role assignments or automation rules; the surrounding infrastructure deployment owns RBAC and automation-rule wiring.
In the Zscaler OneAPI / ZIA admin console, create an OAuth2 API client authorized for the URL/IP category management and status-activation endpoints used by this playbook.

Authorize the Microsoft Teams API connection exactly once after deployment: open the 'teams' connection resource in the Azure portal (or Logic App designer) and complete interactive sign-in/consent for the account that will post and respond to the approval adaptive card. This delegated consent step cannot be automated by an ARM template.

Confirm the Microsoft Sentinel API connection (already configured for managed identity by this template) resolves correctly, and that the Logic App's managed identity has the Microsoft Sentinel Responder role assigned by the surrounding infrastructure deployment.
Only after the previous steps are verified, set WorkflowState to Enabled (or update the deployed resource's state) and attach this playbook to an incident-creation automation rule.
